kinds.d: Lithium tourmaline mineral specimen: the colourful tourmaline species, prized as terminated crystals and slices; gem varieties are named by colour.

x.d: Red to pinkish-red elbaite.
Light blue to bluish-green elbaite.
Green elbaite.
Zoned elbaite with a red or pink centre and green outer zone, often cut as slices.
Colourless elbaite.
Copper-bearing blue to green tourmaline from Brazil, Nigeria and Mozambique; the largest cut stone, 191.87 ct, was shown in Montreal in 2009.
Pink tourmaline from the Stewart mine at Pala (first documented in California in 1890) and the Himalaya mine, San Diego County.
Elbaite from Mount Mica (discovered 1821) and Dunton Quarry on Plumbago Mountain, where the 1972 'Big Find' occurred.
Type-locality elbaite from San Piero in Campo, Elba; named elbaite in 1914 by Vernadsky.
Major locality discovered in 1994 in the Yukon.

kinds.d: Black iron tourmaline mineral specimen: the commonest tourmaline, as striated prisms in quartz and pegmatite.

x.d: Black schorl crystals in white quartz, a classic combination.
Fine black schorl crystals from Erongo, Namibia (Anibib, Farm Etemba).
Schorl from San Piero in Campo, Elba, and Sonnenberg, St Andreasberg, Harz.
Schorl named after Zschorlau, Saxony, called Schorl before 1400; first described as 'schürl' by Mathesius in 1562.
Schorl from Pierrepont and elsewhere in St Lawrence County, New York.

kinds.d: Magnesium tourmaline mineral specimen: brown to yellow-brown crystals, named for the Drava region.

x.d: Fine dravite crystals from Yinnietharra, Western Australia, discovered in the 1970s and now exhausted.
Fine dravite crystals from Gouverneur, Pierrepont and Macomb, St Lawrence County, New York.
Dravite from Brumado, Bahia, Brazil.
Deep green chromium dravite, notably from Tanzania.
Dravite from the Drava region around Dravograd, Slovenia; named by Tschermak in 1884.

kinds.d: Calcium magnesium tourmaline mineral specimen: dark brown to green, named after Uva Province, Sri Lanka.

x.d: Type-locality uvite from Uva Province, Sri Lanka, first found in 1929.
Uvite from Gouverneur, Pierrepont and elsewhere in St Lawrence County, New York.
Uvite from Brumado, Bahia, Brazil.
Uvite from Franklin and Hamburg, Sussex County, New Jersey.

kinds.d: Calcium lithium tourmaline mineral specimen: colour-zoned crystals showing a triangular star in cross-section, from Madagascar.

x.d: Type-locality liddicoatite from Anjanabonoina, Tsilaizina and Antsirabe, Madagascar, named in 1977.
Gemmy colour-zoned crystals from Tsarafara, Sahatany Valley, sometimes with five colour bands.
Slices cut perpendicular to the c axis showing triangular zoning with a trigonal star.

kinds.d: Iron aluminium garnet mineral specimen: deep red dodecahedral and trapezohedral crystals, also in schist.

x.d: Cabochon-cut almandine.
Violet-tinted almandine named for Syriam near Pegu, Myanmar.
Almandine from the gem gravels of Sri Lanka.
Almandine in schist from the Zillertal, Tyrol.
Almandine in mica schist from Wrangell, Alaska.
Large commercial almandine deposit at the Barton mine, North Creek, New York.

kinds.d: Calcium aluminium garnet mineral specimen: green, orange and colourless crystals and massive pink rosolite.

x.d: Intense green to yellowish-green grossular discovered in the Tsavo area of Kenya in the 1960s.
Yellow-red to orange grossular, mainly from Sri Lanka and India placers.
Translucent to opaque pink grossular crystals in marble from Mexico.
Grossular from the Vilyui River, Siberia.
Orange grossular from the Jeffrey mine, Asbestos, Quebec.
Large grossular crystals from Xalostoc and Morelos, Chihuahua, Mexico.

kinds.d: Calcium iron garnet mineral specimen: vivid green demantoid, yellow-green topazolite and black melanite.

x.d: Vivid green andradite, among the most valuable garnets; classic Ural crystals from the Bobrovka River, Nizhny Tagil.
Yellow-green andradite, sometimes gem quality, rarer than demantoid.
Black titanium-bearing andradite.
Andradite from Val Malenco, Lombardy and the Ala Valley, Piedmont.
Andradite from Magnet Cove, Arkansas.

kinds.d: Manganese aluminium garnet mineral specimen: orange to red trapezohedra, with the vivid orange 'Mandarin garnet'.

x.d: Orange-yellow spessartine, from Nigeria and Namibia.
Spessartine from the Ramona and Pala districts, San Diego County, California.
Spessartine from Tsilaizina, Anjanabonoina and the Sahatany valley.
Type-locality spessartine from Aschaffenburg, Spessart Mountains, Bavaria.
Spessartine from the Gilgit district and Dusso, Baltistan, Pakistan.

kinds.d: Calcium chromium garnet mineral specimen: emerald-green crystals, often as a drusy crust on chromite.

x.d: Uvarovite from the Saranowskiy mine, Biserk, Urals, Russia, the type region (named in 1832 by Hess).
Exceptional uvarovite crystals from Outokumpu, Finland, the most significant historical source.
Uvarovite from the Kop Daglari chrome mine, near Aşkale, Turkey.
Uvarovite from the Red Ledge mine and the New Idria area, California.

notes: All 10 planned kinds kept. Fluor-liddicoatite uses HOM liddicoatite and Wikipedia Liddicoatite. Schorl/Dravite Wikipedia pages returned the tourmaline-group article (the Schorl page is cited for group facts). Paraíba not on the Elbaite page but stated on the tourmaline-group page (Schorl URL). Rhodolite left to Gemstones; star garnet not on fetched page. No brands or traditions.
